problemStatement.formal: \text{Formalize Hölder's inequality for finite sums and integrals, showing Cauchy-Schwarz as the p=q=2 special case.}
problemStatement.plain: Prove Hölder's inequality for finite sums (sum f_i*g_i ≤ (sum f_i^p)^(1/p) * (sum g_i^q)^(1/q)) and show that Cauchy-Schwarz ((sum f_i*g_i)^2 ≤ (sum f_i^2)(sum g_i^2)) is the special case p=q=2. Also prove the integral version and the abstract inner product version.
whyMatters: Establishes the full hierarchy: Young → Holder → Cauchy-Schwarz
Connects discrete (finite sums), continuous (integrals), and abstract (inner products) versions
Demonstrates that Cauchy-Schwarz is not an isolated result but a member of a family

insights: The conjugate condition 1/p + 1/q = 1 appears naturally in the Young chain: after applying Young and summing under unit-norm conditions, the sum equals 1/p + 1/q = 1
Cauchy-Schwarz via Lagrange identity: 2*[(sum f^2)(sum g^2) - (sum fg)^2] = sum_i sum_j (f_i*g_j - f_j*g_i)^2 >= 0, proved by expanding and matching cross terms
Holder for real-valued functions: need NNReal lift (cast |f_i| to ℝ≥0), then chain |sum f*g| <= sum|f*g| = sum|f|*|g| <= Holder RHS
Key notation fix: with `open NNReal`, the notation ℝ≥0∞ is shadowed by ℝ≥0 + ∞. Must add `open ENNReal` to make ℝ≥0∞ parse correctly
Proof chain: Young (ab <= a^p/p + b^q/q) -> Normalized Holder -> General Holder -> Cauchy-Schwarz -> Abstract CS -> Integral CS
The file hierarchy: NNReal sums (via Mathlib) -> real sums (via NNReal lift) -> integral (via ENNReal) -> inner product (via norm identity)
